v4-22.candidate: And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, “Come, and I will show you the man you seek.” He went in to her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the peg in his jaw.

v5-2.display:
“When leaders began to lead in Israel,
when the people chose willingly,
bless the Lord!

v5-4.display:
O Lord, when Thou didst go forth from Seir,
when Thou didst depart from the field of Edom,
the earth shook;
heaven was astonished,
and the clouds dropped water.

v5-6.display:
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath,
in the days of Jael,
kings ceased,
and they travelled paths;
they travelled twisted roads.

v5-8.display:
They chose new gods like barley bread.
Would I see a covering of lances among forty thousand?

v5-9.display:
My heart is with the things appointed for Israel.
You mighty ones of the people, bless the Lord!

v5-10.display:
You who ride upon beasts of burden,
you who sit in covered carriages—

v5-11.display:
utter the sound of musicians among those rejoicing.
There they will ascribe righteousness to the Lord.
Righteous people grew strong in Israel;
then the Lord’s people went down to His cities.

v5-12.display:
Awake, awake, Deborah!
Rouse myriads with the people!
Awake, awake, speak with song!
Arise in strength, Barak;
and strengthen Barak, Deborah!
Take your captives, son of Abinoam!

v5-13.display:
When was his strength magnified?
Lord, humble for me those stronger than I am.

v5-14.display:
The people of Ephraim punished them
in the valley of your brother Benjamin, among your peoples.
From me, Machir, investigators came down;
and from Zebulun the Lord fought for me among mighty ones from there,
with a sceptre of one strengthening leadership.

v5-15.display:
In Issachar, with Deborah,
he sent his foot soldiers into the valley.
Why do you dwell between lips?
He stretched out at his feet.
Among the divisions of Reuben were great scrutinies of heart.

v5-16.display:
Why do you sit for me between the mosphathaim,
to hear the whistling of those who rouse?
To pass into the territory of Reuben were great searchings of heart.

v5-17.display:
Gilead camped beyond the Jordan;
and Dan—why does he stay with ships?
Asher stayed by the seashore
and camped by its breaches.

v5-18.display:
Zebulun was a people that scorned its life to the point of death,
and Naphtali on the heights of the field.

v5-20.display:
From heaven the stars fought;
from their appointed order they fought against Sisera.

v5-21.display:
The Kishon torrent cast them out—the torrent Kadēmim, the Kishon torrent.
My mighty soul will trample them.

v5-23.display:
‘Curse Meroz,’ said the Lord’s messenger,
‘utterly curse its inhabitants,
because they did not come to the Lord’s help.
The Lord is our helper, mighty among warriors.’

v5-24.display:
Blessed among women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite;
among women in a tent may she be blessed.

v5-25.display:
He asked her for water, and she gave him milk.
In a bowl of mighty ones she brought butter.

v5-26.display:
She stretched her left hand toward a peg,
her right toward the cuttings of the exhausted;
she cut down Sisera,
crushed his head,
shattered and pierced his jaw.

v5-28.display:
Through the window Sisera’s mother leaned out,
looking through the lattice toward those returning with Sisera:
‘Why is his chariot last to arrive?
Why have the tracks of his chariots been delayed?’

v5-29.display:
The wise among her noble ladies answered her,
and she herself answered in her own words:

v5-30.display:
‘Will they not find him dividing spoils,
befriending friends for the head of a mighty man?
Spoils of dyed cloth for Sisera,
spoils of dyed cloth, embroidery;
a dyed embroidered piece around his neck as spoil.’

v5-31.display:
So perish all Thine enemies, O Lord!
And let those who love Him be as the sun going forth in its might.”

And the land was quiet for forty years.
